examples.ko: 그 사람은 교조적 태도 때문에 친구들과 자주 부딪혀요.
examples.en: He often clashes with his friends because of his dogmatic attitude.

examples.ko: 교조적 사고에서 벗어나야 새로운 생각이 보여요.
examples.en: You have to break free from dogmatic thinking to see new ideas.

examples.ko: 교과서를 교조적 방식으로 가르치면 학생들이 금방 지루해해요.
examples.en: If you teach the textbook in a dogmatic way, students get bored quickly.

examples.ko: 회의에서 교조적 주장만 계속하면 아무도 안 들어요.
examples.en: If you keep making only dogmatic claims in a meeting, nobody will listen.

examples.ko: 저는 규칙을 교조적 해석 없이 상황에 맞게 쓰려고 해요.
examples.en: I try to apply rules to the situation without a dogmatic interpretation.

examples.ko: 교조적 믿음은 사람을 고집스럽게 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: Dogmatic beliefs can make a person stubborn.

explain: '교조적 태도', '교조적 사고'처럼 뒤에 명사가 와요. 이론이나 규칙을 상황과 상관없이 그대로 고집한다는 비판의 느낌이 있어서 좋은 뜻으로는 잘 안 써요. '교조적인'으로도 말하고, 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It goes before a noun, as in '교조적 태도' or '교조적 사고'. It carries criticism: clinging to a theory or rule regardless of the situation, so it is not used as praise. You can also say '교조적인', and it shows up more in news and writing than in casual talk.

examples.ko: 교조주의에 빠지면 현실을 보지 못할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you fall into dogmatism, you may fail to see reality.

examples.ko: 그 교수님은 학계의 교조주의를 늘 비판하셨어요.
examples.en: That professor always criticized dogmatism in academia.

examples.ko: 교조주의 때문에 새로운 의견이 무시되곤 했어요.
examples.en: New opinions used to be ignored because of dogmatism.

examples.ko: 신문 기사에서 교조주의라는 말을 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the word dogmatism for the first time in a newspaper article.
Any theory is dangerous once it drifts into dogmatism.

examples.ko: 교조주의가 강한 모임에서는 의견을 말하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to speak your mind in a group with strong dogmatism.

explain: 정치, 종교, 학문에서 한 가지 이론을 무조건 따르는 태도를 비판할 때 써요. 보통 부정적인 평가이고, 대화보다 글이나 토론에서 많이 나와요. 형용사처럼 쓰고 싶으면 '교조주의적'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used to criticize blindly following one theory in politics, religion or scholarship. It is almost always negative and appears more in writing and debates than in everyday talk. To describe something with it, say '교조주의적'.

examples.ko: 회사가 임원 교체기에 들어서서 분위기가 어수선해요.
examples.en: The company has entered a period of executive turnover, so the mood is unsettled.
Policies change often during a transition of government.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 지금 세대 교체기를 지나고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is going through a generational turnover right now.

examples.ko: 지금은 낡은 시스템의 교체기라서 오류가 자주 나요.
examples.en: It is a period of replacing the old system, so errors happen often.
Employees were very anxious during the transition period.
The confusion of the transition is only temporary.

explain: 계절이 바뀌는 때는 보통 '환절기'라고 하고, '교체기'는 '세대, 정권, 시스템'처럼 앞에 붙은 것이 새것으로 바뀌는 시기에 써요. 시기 전체를 말해서 혼란이나 불안정한 느낌과 함께 나올 때가 많아요.
explain_en: For the change of seasons people usually say '환절기'. '교체기' follows words like generation, government or system and means the period when something is being replaced. It often comes with a sense of confusion or instability.

examples.en: I went to a symphony concert last night.
Listening to symphonic music calms my mind.
This city has a famous symphony orchestra.
I was amazed by the grand sound of the symphony.

examples.ko: 저는 영화 음악보다 교향악이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like symphonic music better than film music.

examples.ko: 교향악처럼 큰 음악은 공연장에서 들어야 제맛이에요.
examples.en: Big music like a symphony is best heard in a concert hall.

explain: 오케스트라가 연주하는 음악을 넓게 가리켜요. 곡 하나를 말할 때는 '교향곡'이라고 해요. 오케스트라는 '교향악단'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers broadly to music played by an orchestra. When you mean one piece, say '교향곡'. An orchestra is also called '교향악단'.

examples.en: There is a small church at the end of the village.
I attend worship at the church every Sunday.

examples.ko: 새 교회당은 건물이 정말 높고 아름다워요.
examples.en: The new church building is really tall and beautiful.
I hear the bell of the old church every morning.
It started raining, so everyone went into the church.

examples.ko: 교회당 건물을 새로 짓는 데 삼 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took three years to build the new church building.

explain: '교회'는 모임과 건물을 다 가리키고, '교회당'은 예배드리는 건물 자체를 말할 때 써요. 천주교의 건물은 '성당'이라고 해요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '교회'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '교회' can mean both the congregation and the building, while '교회당' points to the building itself. A Catholic church building is called '성당'. In daily talk people often just say '교회'.

examples.en: Every word the teacher said is right.

examples.ko: 편지에는 구구절절 어머니의 사랑이 담겨 있었어요.
examples.en: Mother's love was in every line of the letter.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 글은 구구절절 마음에 와닿아요.
examples.en: Every line of his writing touches my heart.
Everything my friend advised was true.

examples.ko: 이유를 구구절절 설명하기가 싫어서 그냥 웃었어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to explain the reason at length, so I just smiled.
You don't need to go on and on; I understand everything.

explain: '구구절절 옳다', '구구절절 맞다'처럼 말이나 글의 모든 부분이 그렇다는 뜻으로 써요. 또 '구구절절 설명하다'처럼 길고 자세하게 늘어놓는다는 뜻으로도 쓰는데, 이때는 조금 귀찮다는 느낌이 있어요. '구구절절이'도 같은 뜻의 부사예요.
explain_en: It is used in '구구절절 옳다' or '구구절절 맞다' to mean every part of what was said or written is so. It is also used in '구구절절 설명하다' to mean explaining at great length, often with a slightly tired feeling. '구구절절이' is an adverb with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 편지 내용이 구구절절해서 읽다가 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: The letter was so heartfelt that I cried while reading it.
That story is so touching.
The long, wordy apology sounds more like an excuse.

examples.ko: 말을 구구절절하게 하지 말고 핵심만 이야기해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't go on and on; just tell me the main point.

examples.ko: 그 선배의 고백은 구구절절하지 않고 짧았어요.
examples.en: The senior's confession was short and not long-winded.
If a story drags on, people get bored listening.

explain: 두 가지로 써요. 하나는 사연이나 편지가 구구절절 마음에 와닿는다는 좋은 뜻이고, 다른 하나는 말이 길고 장황하다는 뜻이에요. 문맥을 보면 어느 쪽인지 알 수 있어요.
explain_en: It has two uses. One is positive: a story or letter that is heartfelt and moving. The other is that speech is long-winded. The context tells you which one it is.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 구김새가 거의 없어서 편해요.
examples.en: This outfit hardly wrinkles, so it is convenient.

examples.ko: 세탁한 뒤에 셔츠의 구김새를 잘 펴 주세요.
examples.en: After washing, please smooth out the creases in the shirt.
I have to iron because of the wrinkles.
The creases go away if you iron them.

examples.ko: 바지 구김새도 괜찮고 색도 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: The way the pants wrinkle is fine, and I like the color too.
Many people care about wrinkles in their clothes.

explain: 옷이나 종이가 구겨진 정도나 모양을 말해요. 일상에서는 '구김'이나 '주름'이라고도 해요. '구김살 없다'는 걱정 없이 밝다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes how much, or in what way, clothes or paper are creased. In daily talk people also say '구김' or '주름'. '구김살 없다' is also used to mean carefree and bright.

examples.en: The shirt got all crumpled inside the bag.
I folded the paper in a crumpled way and put it in my pocket.
I finally found the crumpled receipt.
The child crumpled up the letter and threw it.

examples.ko: 바지가 구깃구깃 주름져서 입고 나갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: The pants are so wrinkled that I can't go out in them.

examples.ko: 옷을 구깃구깃 넣었더니 꺼낼 때 다 구겨져 있어요.
examples.en: I stuffed the clothes in carelessly, so they are all wrinkled when I take them out.

explain: 종이나 옷이 여기저기 마구 구겨진 모습을 나타내요. '구기다', '구겨지다'와 같이 쓰이고, 상태를 말할 때는 '구깃구깃한 옷'처럼 '구깃구깃하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It describes paper or clothes crumpled all over in a messy way. It goes with '구기다' and '구겨지다'. To describe a state, use '구깃구깃하다', as in '구깃구깃한 옷'.

examples.en: These clothes got all wrinkled after I put them in the bag.
I smoothed out the wrinkled shirt with an iron.

examples.ko: 종이가 구깃구깃해서 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The paper is so crumpled that I can't read the writing well.
The handkerchief was folded in a crumpled way.

examples.ko: 옷이 구깃구깃하면 면접에서 인상이 안 좋을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If your clothes are wrinkled, you may make a bad impression at an interview.

examples.ko: 구깃구깃하지 않은 옷을 입고 나가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to go out in clothes that aren't wrinkled.

explain: '구기다'는 누가 구기는 동작이고, '구겨지다'는 구겨지는 변화예요. '구깃구깃하다'는 이미 여기저기 구겨진 상태를 묘사해요. 보통 '구깃구깃한 옷'처럼 뒤에 명사를 꾸며요.
explain_en: '구기다' is the action of crumpling and '구겨지다' is the change of becoming crumpled. '구깃구깃하다' describes the state of already being wrinkled in many places. It usually modifies a noun, as in '구깃구깃한 옷'.

examples.en: My father's cell phone is totally outdated.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 생각이 구닥다리라서 말이 안 통해요.
examples.en: His thinking is so old-fashioned that we can't communicate.
It's an ancient computer, so the programs are very slow.
I was a bit upset to be treated as old-fashioned.

examples.ko: 구닥다리인 줄 알았는데 써 보니 쓸 만해요.
examples.en: I thought it was outdated, but it turns out to be quite usable.
Please don't see me as old-fashioned.

explain: 물건, 생각, 사람에게 다 쓸 수 있어요. 중립적인 '구식'보다 낮추는 느낌이 강해서, 친한 사이에서 농담처럼 쓰거나 윗사람에게는 조심하는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It can be used for objects, ideas and people. It sounds more belittling than the neutral '구식', so it fits jokes among close friends, and you should be careful using it about someone older.

examples.en: The club owner announced a new manager.
This team's owner is a young businessman.
I met the club owner and talked about the contract.

examples.ko: 구단주 때문에 선수들이 팀을 떠나려 해요.
examples.en: Players are trying to leave the team because of the owner.

examples.ko: 새 구단주의 약속을 팬들이 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: The fans are waiting for the new owner's promise.

examples.ko: 구단주에게 편지를 보낸 팬이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A fan who sent a letter to the club owner was on the news.

explain: 야구나 축구 같은 프로 구단을 가진 사람이에요. 스포츠 뉴스에서 '구단주 회의'처럼 많이 나오고, 구단, 감독, 선수와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: This is the person who owns a pro club such as a baseball or soccer team. It appears in sports news in phrases like '구단주 회의', and is good to learn together with 구단, 감독 and 선수.

examples.ko: 여름에 음식을 오래 두면 구더기가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you leave food out for long in summer, maggots appear.
I was shocked to see maggots in the trash can.
There was a terrible smell because of the maggots.
Maggots are the larvae of flies.

examples.ko: 이제 구더기도 없고 냄새도 안 나서 다행이에요.
examples.en: Thankfully, there are no maggots and no smell anymore.
My friend ran away, scared by the maggots.

explain: 파리의 애벌레로, 음식물 쓰레기나 상한 음식에 생겨서 징그러운 느낌이 강해요. 속담 '구더기 무서워 장 못 담글까'에도 나와서 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 조금 힘들 수 있어도 해야 할 일은 해야지, 구더기 무서워 장 못 담글까요?
phrases.en: It might be a bit hard, but we have to do what needs doing; we can't stop just because of a little trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방해가 될 일이 있다고 해서 꼭 필요한 일을 포기하면 안 된다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning you shouldn't give up something necessary just because of possible trouble.
phrases.en_equiv: You can't make an omelette without breaking eggs.

explain_en: These are fly larvae that appear in food waste or spoiled food, and the word feels disgusting. It also appears in the proverb '구더기 무서워 장 못 담글까', which is worth knowing.

examples.ko: 그는 실패한 뒤 절망의 구렁텅이에 빠졌어요.
examples.en: After failing, he fell into the depths of despair.

examples.ko: 나쁜 습관 때문에 게으름의 구렁텅이에서 못 나왔어요.
examples.en: Because of a bad habit, I couldn't get out of the pit of laziness.
Be careful not to fall into the abyss.

examples.ko: 가난의 구렁텅이는 쉽게 벗어날 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The pit of poverty was not easy to escape.
He worked hard to climb out of the hole he was in.
Even in the depths, I didn't let go of hope.

explain: 깊고 험한 구덩이라는 뜻도 있지만, 주로 '절망의 구렁텅이', '가난의 구렁텅이'처럼 헤어나기 힘든 나쁜 상황을 비유해요. '빠지다', '벗어나다'와 같이 쓰이고 말보다는 글에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It can mean a deep, rough pit, but it is mostly used figuratively for a bad situation that is hard to escape, as in '절망의 구렁텅이' or '가난의 구렁텅이'. It pairs with '빠지다' and '벗어나다' and appears more in writing than speech.

examples.en: My father wears long sideburns.
My sideburns are long, so I need to go to the barber.
That actor's sideburns look cool.
The sideburns run from in front of the ear down to the chin.
Now that you've grown sideburns too, you look different.

examples.ko: 구레나룻에 흰 털이 조금 섞여 있어요.
examples.en: There are a few white hairs mixed into the sideburns.

explain: 귀 밑에서 턱까지 이어서 난 수염을 말해요. 입 위의 '콧수염', 턱에 난 '턱수염'과 구별해서 써요. 발음은 [구레나룯]이에요.
explain_en: This is the beard growing from below the ears down to the chin. Keep it separate from '콧수염' (mustache) and '턱수염' (chin beard). It is pronounced [구레나룯].

examples.en: We did exercises in time with the teacher's commands.
Please call out the commands loudly.
The sound of commands echoed across the playground.
The commands were so fast that it was hard to keep up.
Commands are short, like 'one, two'.

examples.ko: 구령으로 시작하는 아침 체조 시간이 좋았어요.
examples.en: I liked the morning exercise time that started with commands.

explain: 체육 시간, 군대, 행사에서 여럿이 동작을 맞추려고 외치는 말이에요. '구령을 붙이다', '구령에 맞추다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: These are the calls shouted so that many people move in unison, in PE class, the military or events. Typical combinations are '구령을 붙이다' and '구령에 맞추다'.

examples.en: When prices rise, consumers' purchasing power falls.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 구매력 높은 중산층이 많아요.
examples.en: This country has many middle-class people with high purchasing power.

examples.ko: 월급이 같아도 환율에 따라 구매력은 달라져요.
examples.en: Even with the same salary, purchasing power changes with the exchange rate.

examples.ko: 정부는 청년의 구매력을 높일 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is looking for ways to raise young people's purchasing power.

examples.ko: 구매력에 맞는 가격으로 물건을 팔아야 해요.
examples.en: You have to sell goods at prices that match what customers can afford.

examples.ko: 구매력까지 고려하면 이 도시가 더 비싸요.
examples.en: If you take purchasing power into account too, this city is more expensive.

explain: 가진 돈으로 물건을 살 수 있는 힘이에요. 월급이 같아도 물가가 오르면 구매력은 떨어져요. 단순한 소득이나 재산과는 달라요. '구매력이 높다/낮다/떨어지다', '구매력을 높이다'처럼 경제 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means how much you can buy with the money you have. Even with the same salary, purchasing power drops when prices rise, so it differs from income or wealth itself. It is common in economic news, as in '구매력이 높다/낮다/떨어지다' and '구매력을 높이다'.
